answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks through cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs, which tether identity to scarce hardware origins. Rather than letting rogue nodes cluster like a dense nebula or isolate into an unaccountable island, verification deposits demand exponential capital exhaustion for Sybil swarms. This creates a velvet chokehold where scaling fake identities imposes superlinear, ruinous attacker cost.
